samples.summary: Untrusted shape `data.kind` is interpolated into the OOXML `prst` attribute with no allowlist and no escaping — reachable from the v1 content PUT API that this change now walks
samples.evidence: `kindToPrst(kind)` returns the model value verbatim (`return kind === 'pentagonArrow' ? 'homePlate' : kind;`) and it is interpolated raw at shape.ts:94 `<a:prstGeom prst="${kindToPrst(data.kind)}">`. `ShapeKind` is a type-only union, so the value is whatever JSON was persisted. Attack: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content with `{"meta":{...},"themes":[],"masters":[],"layouts":[],"slides":[{"id":"s","layoutId":"l","background":{},"notes":[],"elements":[{"id":"e","type":"shape","frame":{},"data":{"kind":"rect\"/><a:evil x=\""}}]}]}`. The new `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:504-556) walks exactly this element and validates only `data.text` block styles, so `data.kind` passes; `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:105) stores `slides` verbatim. Any later PPTX export by a viewer emits attacker-chosen XML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml. This is the same sink class the change hardened for `w:jc`/`algn`/`srgbClr val`, missed here.

samples.summary: The new slides-arm block-style validation is bypassable within the same endpoint: `slides[].notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements` and `masters[]` hold the same docs Block/Element shapes and are persisted verbatim with no validation at all
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only does `Array.isArray(s.notes)` (controller.ts:490-494) yet `Slide.notes` is `Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) — the same docs blocks that reach the same layout engine and are exported through `notesSlideToXml` → `textBodyToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:205). `assertValidSlidesBody` (controller.ts:452-458) checks only that `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays, and `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:102-105) assigns all four verbatim; `Layout.placeholders` is `ElementInit[]` carrying text bodies (presentation.ts:56-63). So a caller rejected for `slides[0].elements[0].data.blocks[0].style.alignment` can store the identical value in the same request via `slides[0].notes[0].style.alignment` or `layouts[0].placeholders[0].data.blocks[0].style`. docs/design/rest-api.md advertises the check for 'the docs Blocks inside every text body', so the gate reads as coverage it does not have.

samples.summary: `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` is still a prototype-walking object-literal lookup with no own-key guard and no fallback — the exact hazard this change replaced with `Map` in ALGN / UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U / DOCX_ALIGNMENTS
samples.evidence: `const val = ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role];` then `<a:schemeClr val="${val}"/>` (color.ts:49-50). `text.ts` guards its own callers via `Object.keys(ROLE_TO_SCHEME).includes(c.role)`, but `fillXml`/`solidFillXml`/`gradFillXml` (color.ts:63-94) pass model-supplied `ThemeColor`s (shape fill, background fill, gradient stops) whose `role` is unvalidated persisted JSON from the content PUT API / PPTX import. An unknown role yields `val="undefined"`; a prototype key such as `constructor`/`toString` yields the native function source. No quote characters appear in those strings, so I could not complete an injection chain — the impact I can demonstrate is a schema-invalid attribute plus a latent injection sink if the map ever carries a value with reserved characters.

samples.summary: `headingLevel` is still interpolated raw into `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` in the same function whose sibling `w:jc` attribute was hardened this change
samples.evidence: docx-style-map.ts:134-136 emits `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` with no coercion or escaping, while the `alignment` two lines below was routed through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map precisely because 'the value reaching an exporter is whatever string was persisted into the CRDT'. `headingLevel` is equally untrusted: the content PUT API does not validate it (controller.ts:340-423 checks id/type/style/inlines only) and `buildBlockNode` persists `String(block.headingLevel)` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:241). A non-numeric string here would inject arbitrary XML into document.xml / header1.xml. Confidence is low because both readers coerce with `Number(attrs.headingLevel)` (docs-tree.ts:396, yorkie-doc-store.ts:473), so I could not close the chain from the API to the exporter; a direct Document→DocxExporter path (import/CLI/paste) would.

samples.summary: `tag in HEADING_MAP` resolves prototype keys, so pasted HTML with a `<constructor>`/`<tostring>` element produces a non-numeric `headingLevel` that is persisted and later interpolated into the DOCX `w:pStyle` attribute
samples.evidence: clipboard.ts:130-132: `if (tag in HEADING_MAP) return { type: 'heading', headingLevel: HEADING_MAP[tag] };` — `in` consults `Object.prototype`, and `tag` is `el.tagName.toLowerCase()` from attacker-supplied pasted HTML. `HEADING_MAP['constructor']` yields the `Object` function, which `makeBlock` (clipboard.ts:108) stores as `headingLevel`, `String(block.headingLevel)` persists into the Tree, and `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` interpolates into `w:val`. The native-function source contains no reserved XML characters, so this is corruption rather than a demonstrated injection, but it is the same prototype-chain lookup the change fixed elsewhere and it is the feeder for the raw `w:pStyle` sink above.

samples.summary: The newly added group / nested-table validator walks recurse without a depth bound on a 25 MB request body — a deeply nested payload can exhaust the stack inside the validator
samples.evidence: `assertValidElement` recurses into `data.children` (controller.ts:550-555) and `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` recurses into `tableData.rows[].cells[]` (controller.ts:607-621), with no depth cap; `assertValidBlock` does the same for docs table cells. `bodyParser.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT })` with `JSON_BODY_LIMIT = '25mb'` (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20,49) allows a payload nested tens of thousands of levels deep. A single authenticated request can then throw RangeError from inside the handler (500) after burning CPU, and repeated requests are a cheap amplification. Low confidence because V8's JSON.parse may reject some depths first; I did not measure the crossover.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element verified in-tree. shape.ts:16-18 `kindToPrst` returns the model string verbatim and shape.ts:94 interpolates it into `<a:prstGeom prst="...">` with no escaping — while the very same function escapes other attacker-influenced attributes via `escapeXmlAttr` (shape.ts:117, shape.ts:164, xml.ts:5), confirming the omission is real rather than an intentional trusted-value path. `ShapeKind` (model/element.ts:54, used at element.ts:349) is a compile-time-only union, and `migrateElement` (model/migrate.ts:156-167) only normalizes `data.fill`, spreading everything else through, so no runtime allowlist constrains `kind` on read. On the ingest side, `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:504-556) validates `id`/`type`/`frame` and, for `type === 'shape'`, only recurses into `data.text` (lines 534-538); `data.kind` is never examined. The PUT handler (docs-content.controller.ts:126-198) then calls `writeSlidesRoot`, which does `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (yorkie/slides-tree.ts:105). Result: a persisted `kind` such as `rect"/><a:evil x="` breaks out of the attribute and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml for any later exporter/viewer. This is XML/template injection into a generated document — in the Security lens's injection lane. It requires document-write access rather than being unauthenticated, which is consistent with the reviewer's `major` (not critical) rating; I found no guard, allowlist, or escaping anywhere on the path that would make it unreachable.

finding.summary: The new slides-arm block-style validation is bypassable within the same endpoint: `slides[].notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements` and `masters[]` hold the same docs Block/Element shapes and are persisted verbatim with no validation at all
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only does `Array.isArray(s.notes)` (controller.ts:490-494) yet `Slide.notes` is `Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) — the same docs blocks that reach the same layout engine and are exported through `notesSlideToXml` → `textBodyToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:205). `assertValidSlidesBody` (controller.ts:452-458) checks only that `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays, and `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:102-105) assigns all four verbatim; `Layout.placeholders` is `ElementInit[]` carrying text bodies (presentation.ts:56-63). So a caller rejected for `slides[0].elements[0].data.blocks[0].style.alignment` can store the identical value in the same request via `slides[0].notes[0].style.alignment` or `layouts[0].placeholders[0].data.blocks[0].style`. docs/design/rest-api.md advertises the check for 'the docs Blocks inside every text body', so the gate reads as coverage it does not have.

verdict.reason: The reviewer's code facts check out (notes/layouts/masters are only array-checked at docs-content.controller.ts:452-458 and :490-494, and writeSlidesRoot assigns them verbatim at slides-tree.ts:102-105), but this is not a Security-lens defect. (a) No trust boundary is crossed: the endpoint is behind CombinedAuthGuard + WorkspaceScopeGuard (controller.ts:74) and the caller is writing content into a document they are already authorized to write; the validator's own docstring states its purpose is returning 400 instead of 500 (controller.ts:132-141, 426-431), i.e. it is a shape guard, not an authz/integrity control. (b) The only sink where an unvalidated style value could become a security issue — OOXML emission — is already hardened against precisely this input, and notes flow through it: notesSlideToXml wraps notes into a TextBody and calls the same textBodyToXml (export/pptx/slide.ts:205-207), where alignment is resolved through a prototype-safe Map with fallback (`ALGN.get(...) ?? 'l'`, text.ts:69-74, 99 — comment explicitly names the content PUT API as the untrusted source), numeric style fields are coerced/rounded so a NaN/string yields `marL="NaN"` rather than attribute breakout (text.ts:105-123), list level is clamped (text.ts:82-86), and free-form strings are escaped (escapeXmlText/escapeXmlAttr, text.ts:168, 236, 240, 325, 335). Layouts are equally safe: layoutToXml escapes the name (export/pptx/layout.ts:54) and emits no placeholder shapes at all (layout.ts:48-50, 65-68). No innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink consumes this data in packages/slides. Residual impact is a malformed style or NaN in the caller's own deck — correctness/design-fit, not authz, secrets, injection, or crypto.
